 Panthers Forward, which has helped 1,350 Pitt seniors address their student loans, welcomes its 9th class
 November 19, 2026 
 Tags 
 Cultivate student success 
 Subscribe to Pittwire Today
 Get the most interesting and important stories from the University of Pittsburgh.
 Subscribe
 The University of Pittsburgh’s Panthers Forward program, which has helped 1,350 students address nearly $6.75 million in federal student loan debt over the last nine years, welcomed 150 seniors to its Class of 2027 this fall.
 Panthers Forward is a first-of-its-kind program open to eligible students on the University’s Pittsburgh campus who use federal loans to fund their last year of college. Participants receive up to $5,000 in direct federal student loan relief, mentoring from Pitt alumni, and exclusive access to events, workshops and financial planning resources.
 After graduation, participants are encouraged to pay it forward to the next generation, whether through financial support or by sharing their time and talents.
 “The students selected for Panthers Forward have worked incredibly hard to reach their final year at Pitt,” said Sarah Cullen, who directs the program. “Through this program, we can provide financial support, resources and connections that help them take their next steps more confidently. It is inspiring to see each new class join a community of alumni and mentors who are committed to lifting one another up and creating opportunities for Panthers.”
 The newest class gathered on Nov. 3 for a welcome and networking event, where students posed for professional headshots, learned about financial planning and connected with classmates and mentors.
 Meet the full Class of 2027 . Applications for the Class of 2028 will open in September 2027.
 Photography by Lisa Eggleston
